sections.title: Understanding the Problem
points: Build a brokerage-facing application that streams stock prices and submits customer orders to external trading infrastructure.
Displayed prices, submitted orders, exchange acknowledgements, and executions are distinct records with different timing guarantees.

sections.title: Functional Requirements
points: View live stock prices and manage stock orders.
Track order status and resulting account changes.
Integrate with external market-data and execution services rather than designing an exchange matching engine.

sections.title: Non-functional Requirements
points: Keep market-data updates responsive while preserving correct and durable order state.
Avoid duplicate order submission after retries and recover ambiguous external outcomes.
Scale popular-symbol fanout independently from the transactional order path.

sections.title: Core Entities
points: Account and Position represent ownership and reserved or available funds/holdings.
Order stores customer intent, symbol, side, quantity, type, limit price where applicable, and lifecycle state.
Execution records a fill, including quantity, price, external ID, and time.
Quote stores symbol, price information, source sequence, and timestamp.

sections.title: API
points: Subscribe to prices for a set of symbols and fetch a current snapshot.
Submit an order with a stable client request ID; return an order ID and current acceptance state.
Query orders and positions and request cancellation of an eligible order.
Treat cancellation as a request until external confirmation; an order may fill while cancellation is in flight.

sections.title: 1) Live prices
points: Ingest market feeds once, normalize updates, and cache the latest value by symbol.
Connection servers subscribe to symbols needed by their clients and fan updates out locally.
Separate market-data ingestion from browser connections so reconnecting clients do not create new external feed subscriptions.
Include timestamps or sequence information so clients can detect stale or reordered updates.

flows.title: Distribute a market-price update
steps: The market-data adapter receives an external quote, validates its source ordering, and normalizes the symbol and fields.
It updates the latest quote cache and publishes the new version to the symbol's shared channel.
Connection servers subscribed to that symbol receive the event once for their local interested clients.
They send or coalesce display updates according to the freshness policy, and clients ignore older versions.
A reconnecting client fetches a current snapshot before resuming live updates rather than replaying an unlimited stale-price backlog.

sections.title: 2) Orders
points: Validate the authenticated account, order parameters, and available buying power or holdings.
Persist the order and required reservation before submitting to the external execution path.
Use stable external/client order identifiers to reconcile retries and avoid duplicate orders.
Apply execution reports to durable order, cash, and position state with idempotent processing.

flows.title: Submit and process a stock order
steps: The customer sends side, symbol, quantity, order type, and a stable client request ID to the order API.
The service authenticates the account, validates the order, and checks for an existing request result.
Within the account/order consistency boundary, it reserves the required buying power or holdings and persists a pending order.
After that commit, a recoverable submission worker sends the order to external execution infrastructure using the stable external order identity.
The service records external acknowledgement or rejection. Local request acceptance is not a claim that the exchange has accepted or filled the order.
Execution reports update filled quantity, cash, positions, and remaining reservations idempotently; partial fills leave the remainder open according to order rules.
Only committed transitions are sent to the customer. A submission timeout triggers status reconciliation before any potentially duplicate external resubmission.

sections.title: 1) Scale price delivery
points: Popular symbols create hot channels; share subscriptions across clients and replicate fanout capacity.
Coalesce updates where the product only needs the latest displayed price, without dropping authoritative execution events.
Bound slow-client buffers and provide a fresh snapshot after reconnect rather than replaying an unlimited stale-price backlog.

sections.title: 2) Track order updates
points: Model pending, acknowledged, partially filled, filled, cancelled, and rejected states explicitly.
Deduplicate external events using execution/report IDs and preserve cumulative filled quantities.
Reconcile against the external provider when an acknowledgement or status update is missing.
Publish customer-facing updates after committing state so a notification cannot claim a fill that was never recorded.

flows.title: Handle cancellation racing a fill
steps: The customer requests cancellation of an eligible open order; the service records the request without immediately declaring the order cancelled.
The execution adapter submits the cancellation using the provider's order identity.
Meanwhile, any execution report is applied by its unique fill/report ID, including fills arriving before cancellation takes effect.
When external cancellation is confirmed, the service closes the unfilled remainder and releases only its remaining reserved funds or securities.
The final customer state includes actual fills plus the cancelled remainder; it never erases a completed fill because a cancellation was requested first.

sections.title: 3) Order consistency
points: Reserve funds or securities atomically with accepting the relevant order intent.
Partial fills, cancellation, and rejection release or consume only the remaining reserved amount.
A timeout does not prove the provider rejected the order; query status before deciding whether resubmission is safe.
Keep an auditable history of transitions rather than overwriting all evidence with the latest status.

sections.title: Final Design
points: A dedicated market-data pipeline handles snapshots and high-volume price fanout.
A durable order state machine coordinates account reservations, external submission, and execution reports.
Idempotency and reconciliation handle the uncertainty inherent in external trading systems.
